The present DAR arises out of road accident in which one Vidhan Biswas, aged about 26 years, suffered injuries. In terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act, the same is treated as a claim petition. Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through DD no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road, investigating officer reached the spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was found flipped on the middle of the road. The person injured had been taken to the hospital by then. On reaching the hospital, one of the injured Ganesh Das stated that on 07.11.2021 at 03:00 p.m., he was travelling along with 13 other people in the offending vehicle. After performing religious ritual (idol immersion) near Yamuna River, at Sarai Kale Khan, all the 13 passengers boarded the offending vehicle for returning to Bengali Camp. When the offending tempo reached near Najaf Khan Tomb, Najaf Khan Road, Lodhi Road, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 started driving the vehicle at very high speed recklessly. Despite being cautioned he kept driving the Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.10.21 04:24:22 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 2 of 25(ss) vehicle negligently at high speed, due to which the offending vehicle flipped off, causing injury to its passengers and death of the son of the petitioner. It is further pleaded that there is a possibility that the offending vehicle may have been planted to raise a false claim. It is however not denied that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 vide policy no. RL2012070054 for the period from 07.12.2020 to 06.12.2021. texts.facts: 3. An FIR No. 206/2021 dated 07.11.2021 u/s 188/279/269/337/338/304A of IPC & Section 3 Epidemic Disease Act was registered at PS Lodhi Colony. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. In response to the DAR, insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle. It is further pleaded that even the injured Vidhan Biswas was found to be under influence of alcohol. It is pleaded that since the offending vehicle could be used only as a light goods carriage vehicle, petitioner was an unauthorized /gratuitous passenger along with 13 other persons, all of whom were it violation of the Covid-19 pandemic (DDMA guidelines) guidelines and thus not entitled to compensation. Despite opportunity, no reply was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 or respondent no.2. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.01.2023. OPP. 3) Relief. 6. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/Vidhan Biswas examined himself as PW-1. He relied upon his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the factum and manner of the accident. He deposed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1. He further relied upon his MLC prepared at AIIMS Trauma Center as de exhibited and marked as Mark A, original discharge summary as Ex.PW1/2, his medical treatment records as Ex.PW1/3(colly), original medical bills as Ex.PW1/4(colly), his Adhar Card as mark B, his PAN card Mark C and copy of his 10 th class marksheet as Mark D. He deposed that on account of being bedridden for about 5 month due to the accident, he had to incur medical expenditure of Rs.10,000/-, Rs.25,000/- towards special diet and Rs.30,000/- towards conveyance. He deposed that at the time of the accident he was 26 years of age and was doing a private job in Delhi and earning Rs.35,000/- to 36,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he lost his job and earnings. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Upon closing of petitioner evidence, respondent no.1 led his evidence by examining himself as RW1. RW1 Akendra Kumar examined himself his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R1W1/A. In his examination in chief, he stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. He stated that none of the alleged victims were travelling in the offending vehicle. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.R1W1/1. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. Such cross examination was adopted by ld. Counsel for petitioners. 8. In respondent evidence, the owner of the offending vehicle /respondent no.2 also examined himself as RW2/Sh. Bhanu Prakash Sharma. He relied upon his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2WA and his identity card as Ex.R2W2/1. RW2 also denied involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and pleaded the FIR to be false and concocted. liability to pay compensation, if any, lies upon the insurance company with which his vehicle was insured. 9. Insurance company /respondent no.3 also examined its witness Sh. Parth Arya as R3W1. R3W1 relied upon his evidence Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:24:39 Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 5 of 25(ss) by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 wherein he testified that as per the Registration Certificate, the offending vehicle was a light goods vehicle with a seating capacity of 3 persons. It is pleaded that the said vehicle was being used for transportation of passengers, beyond its permitted capacity, in violation of the permit. He testified that since the respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by violating the RC and permit, the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.R3W1/1, attested copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/3 and DAR /FIR /chargesheet/RC/Route Permit as already Ex.PW1/6 (colly). He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and 2. 10.
texts.arguments: It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that since petitioner has suffered injury on account of accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured, may be directed to compensate the petitioner. On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioner has failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date: MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 6 of 04:25:11 25(ss) +0530 compensate the petitioner. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e. respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims.
